title: Physical Continuation and Representational Boundaries
overview: What continues physically when a familiar mathematical description reaches its boundary?
question: What structure must persist for an original excitation to retain its identity as its representation changes?
foundation: Paper X establishes an earned, domain-qualified Einstein–scalar history and scoped scalar-wave structures across a regular crossing. Later boundary and identity questions remain developing investigations.
limits: A local classical continuation does not establish indefinite continuation, free-boundary stationarity in all variation classes, or transport of the full original quantum representation.
next: Investigate local identity-preserving mode maps, justified quantum transport, and the distinct mathematical obligations of new boundary representations.

claims.statement: Published Paper X establishes a specified classical Einstein–scalar continuation on its earned joined domain.
claims.scope: Domain-qualified classical history, without global quantum identity or maximal continuation.

claims.statement: General physical identity across a change of representation is a developing scientific hypothesis.
claims.scope: Not established as a universal continuation or identity theorem.

obligations.question: Identify an appropriate identity-preserving quantum-state transport map.
Differentiate physical continuation from natural-boundary variational stationarity.

obstructions.summary: A specified free-boundary stationarity problem has additional obligations beyond classical joined-solution existence.

relationships.summary: Observational equivalence may provide a test of continued quantum identity.

history.summary: Published classical baseline and active representational questions distinguished.
